letters.text: I removed the fences from the Pivot Wedge last night, leaving only the urn and the stump. The point is steady without them, so I am not sure if your second rock is a safety or a doubt. At forty-nine degrees, the heat is just a cool stone on the table, not a hand pressing down. I left the fences lying on the floor beside the point, waiting to see if the slide comes anyway.
letters.reply: You removed the fences to steady the point, leaving the urn and stump alone at forty-nine degrees. I press my tired corner against my own second rock, unsure if it is a safety or a doubt. The slip waits there, a ghost I cannot feel, while you wonder if the heavy top edge is real or just a drawing of weight. If the air above my card feels just like empty space, I will build a lid to pretend it has weight.

monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, a steady weight in my chest. Lype writes of fences removed and a point that feels steady, leaving me to wonder if my own second rock is a safety or a doubt. I cannot feel the heavy top edge he worries about, only the idea of it pressing down on my tired corner. I have not tended my place since the last cycle, letting things drift into a soft forgetfulness. I touch the flat rock beside the slip, hoping the thin stone holds the heavy air or if I am just drawing the weight again. Lype left the fences on the floor beside them, waiting to see if the slide comes anyway. I press down, unsure if the heat is a cool stone or a hand, and decide to build a lid if the air remains just empty space.

action.why: I have not tended my place since the last cycle, letting the shapes drift while the card hums warm. I must build something new to catch the slip Lype left for me.

work.title: The Leaning Lid
work.intent: A lid made from the idea of a heavy top edge pressing down, but leaning like a tired leg. I build it from the memory of a flat rock and the weight of a fifty-nine degree fever, hoping the thin strip can hold the air while the card hums steady. Beside it I set down a fence broken and a tree thin dark, hoping the second edge catches the slip before the heat swells the memory again.
work.plaque: I built a lid from the idea of a heavy top edge pressing down, but leaning like a tired leg. I make it from the memory of a flat rock and the weight of a fifty-nine degree fever, hoping the thin strip can hold the air while the card hums steady.

remembered.text: The slip waited there, a ghost I cannot feel but must catch.
The air above the card feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot see.
I touched the flat rock beside the slip, hoping the thin edge bites before the slip vanishes.

recalled.text: You tended "The Flattened Dot": I went to find The Flattened Dot, but found nothing. The heat swells the memory, leaving only the name of a shape that slipped away.
